blockNote: Runtime pull / collect interaction handlers (Bank 00): three small actor scripts spawned with SpawnAfterMarked as children of a gem or a movable solid (collect_handler_gem, push_handler_solid, push_handler_forceball).

The child's $04 (prevActorLink) is the actor it was marked after, i.e. the object being moved (the 'parent'). The handler reads the player position ($0014 / $0016 of playerActor) and edits the parent's posX / posY ($14 / $16). Its own $14 / $16 start as a copy of the parent's (CopyActorState) and are used as the reference position for every distance test.
=== SHARED STRUCTURE ===
1. SetSavedPtr( &self ) keeps the idle entry in retPtr1 ($7F0004). RestoreSavedPtr later resumes there (and clears retPtr1), which re-arms the handler. Every 'Restore' label below is that exit.

2. SetEntryHereAndYield + BranchIfPressed( #$0031 ): bit 0 of the mask selects joypadRaw, and $0030 is the L / R shoulder pair (the guard / channel button; player_character BlockStopToIdle tests the same $0030 for 'L/R released'). Not held: RTL, poll again next frame.
3. BranchIfPlayerNear( #0F ): radius 15 tiles, a square |dx| and |dy| < 241 px. A coarse gate only.

4. BranchOnPlayerX( #$000F, ... ): the engine handler (cop_handlers_player_query) loads operand slot +2 when the player is more than 15 px WEST of the actor, +6 when more than 15 px EAST and +4 when within 15 px (including 0). The slot +4 operand is therefore 'player in the same column', and in this file it leads to the block that works on the Y axis ($0016, posY). BranchOnPlayerY does the same for the row and leads to the blocks that work on posX ($0014).
(docs/cop/families/player_query.md and the copdef label the three operands West / East / Here, but the handler's order is West / Here / East; see OQ-I037-3.)

5. Each axis block computes d = player - own position. d < 0 means the player is above (Y blocks) or west of (X blocks) the object. |d| is needed, then GetPlayerFacingDirection must report that the player faces the object (codes 0 down, 1 up, 2 left, 3 right), then the object is moved ONE direction: toward the player. These handlers therefore pull the object to the player; the 'push' in the old names and header was a guess.

6. The label pairs are named after the wrong axis: *AlignWest / *MoveWest and *AlignEast / *MoveEast are the vertical blocks (player above / below), *AlignNorth / *MoveNorth and *AlignSouth / *MoveSouth are the horizontal ones (player west / east). Each block's second BPL after the first BPL is dead (N is still set), so the abs() always runs for d < 0.
=== HANDLERS ===

collect_handler_gem: no clearance test and no collision painting. Step count = |d| / 2 (kept in orbitAngle, $7F0010,X). After the first facing test it SetEntryHere's, so the following frames skip the button / facing tests and move the parent 2 px per frame (parent posY / posX -/+ 2, own copy updated too) until the count reaches zero, then restore idle. The old header said it nudges the player; it moves the parent (the gem) and only reads the player.

push_handler_solid: needs |d| >= $20 (32 px), BranchIfSolidOffset( dx, dy ) one tile toward the player clear (any lower-nibble bit set = blocked), ClearSolidHere, own pos -/+ $10, MarkSolidHere (collision moves at once), SFX $2C, then parent $12 bit $0010 is set (old state kept in $24) while LoopStart( $10 ) slides the parent 1 px per pass (16 passes = one tile), then the bit is restored. $12 bit $0010 is damage / stagger immunity in combat_collision (the wram map calls it push-in-progress). The check state skips a frame when the parent's $10 bit $0080 (victim iframe flag) is set and $12 bit $0010 is clear.

push_handler_forceball: same distance and facing tests, but additionally the player's sprite index ($28) must be $3A (player above the ball), $3B (below), $3D (west) or $3C (east), the poses that match down / up / left / right. It uses NudgePosition( dx, dy ) on its own position instead of Clear / MarkSolidHere, and while the button is not held it copies the parent's posX / posY every frame.

Spawn sites (SpawnAfterMarked): collect_handler_gem - DarkGemDropSystem (3), field_reveal_object, ec0B_cell (prison cell); push_handler_solid - gw82_archer (2), ir26_statue, ir20_statue, ir1F_stone_lord, ir1F_stone_guard, ec0E_statue, sc02_seth, sg51_statue, sg4D_knight_armor (2); push_handler_forceball - mu60_force_ball.
UNVERIFIED-RUNTIME: that the object really moves toward the player in play and which in-game action the L / R + facing pose is.

collect_handler_gem: Idle loop for a collectable gem: arm, poll L / R, gate on 15 tiles, then the same-column / same-row dispatch (see the block note).
CollectGemAlignWest: Same-column block (player above or below). d = player posY - own posY. d < 0: player above, so the facing code must be 0 (down); the gem then moves up 2 px per frame.
CollectGemAlignEast: d >= 0: player at or below the gem; facing must be 1 (up); the gem moves down 2 px per frame.
CollectGemAlignNorth: Same-row block (player west or east). d = player posX - own posX. d < 0: player west, facing must be 3 (right); the gem moves west 2 px per frame.
CollectGemAlignSouth: d >= 0: player east of the gem; facing must be 2 (left); the gem moves east 2 px per frame.
push_handler_solid: Idle loop for a pullable solid: same arm / poll / gate preamble as the gem handler.
PushSolidCheckState: Skips this frame (RTL) while the parent has $10 bit $0080 (iframe-active per combat_collision) and does not carry $12 bit $0010.
PushSolidMoveWest: Same-column block (player above or below the solid): needs |posY delta| >= $20, facing 0 (down), tile one row up free; the solid moves up one tile.
PushSolidMoveEast: Player below the solid: facing 1 (up), tile one row down free; the solid moves down one tile.
PushSolidMoveNorth: Same-row block (player west or east): needs |posX delta| >= $20, facing 3 (right), tile one column west free; the solid moves west one tile.
PushSolidMoveSouth: Player east of the solid: facing 2 (left), tile one column east free; the solid moves east one tile.
PushSolidSetPushingFlag: Parent $12 |= $0010 for the slide. The previous value of that bit goes to $24 (this handler's scratch); returns with RTS.
PushSolidClearPushingFlag: Parent $12 = ($12 and $FFEF) or the saved bit in $24, i.e. restore the state from before the slide.
push_handler_forceball: Force-ball variant: also needs the matching player pose ($28 = $3A..$3D) and mirrors the parent position while idle.

blockNote: Shared init JSL used by only two actors: dm3F_laborer (code_0AA9E0, Diamond Mine) and fr32_kidnapper (Freejia). The older header said 'most enemy actors'.

Sets $12 |= $0030 (TSB): in combat_collision $12 bit $0010 is damage / stagger immunity and bit $0020 is 'boss' (damage digits and the player-attack hit test are skipped). The older 'solid + interactable' label has no reader behind it.

Sets extendedFlags ($7F002A,X) |= $0080, which the OrExtraFlags notes in cop_handlers_callbacks identify as the boss bit (not 'enemy type'), points statsPtr ($7F0020,X) at enemy_stats_table and sets currentHp ($7F0026,X) = 1.
fr32_kidnapper overwrites currentHp with 5 right after the JSL. Whether the damage code replaces the HP with a stats-table lookup on the first hit was not traced (UNVERIFIED-RUNTIME).

blockNote: Actor entry code that places the actor at a random point within -128..+127 px of the player on each axis.
Not a JSL helper: awB1_goldcap and pyDD_mummy_queen spawn it with SpawnAfterMarked( @RandomPlayerOffset, #$2000 ) and keep the child slot (TYA, then STA $26 / scratch1010+6).

posX ($14) = playerXPos + (RngByte - $80), posY ($16) = playerYPos + (RngByte - $80), then $08 = $3C. $08 is the wait counter (wram-memory-map), so the actor sleeps 60 frames; its entry pointer is never changed, so it should run this code again and re-roll the position: a marker that hops every 60 frames, not a '60-frame lifetime' as the older header said.
UNVERIFIED-RUNTIME: the rerun from the unchanged $00 after the wait. unused_random_position_noref is an unreferenced sibling without the player offset.
